messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the reshuffle wasn’t chaos—it was a playbook. The security forces are hiring consultants, not digging trenches, and the business crowd is quietly moving assets like they’re bracing for a storm, not a collapse. The regime’s too confident for panic, but the streets? People are whispering like they *want* to believe something’s coming. Still—no one’s moved yet. But when the money starts running faster than the rumors, we’ll know."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—cabinet’s moving like clockwork, but the boots on the ground are dragging their feet. Memes are flying, the shops are restless, and the regime’s suddenly *very* interested in PR… but the garbage isn’t getting picked up on time. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a storm or just the wind, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the regime’s still holding things together—for now. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to jump, and the top brass is still playing the same old game of carrots and sticks. The real question is whether they’re bluffing about how strong they are, or if the opposition’s just waiting for someone else to blink first. Either way, the air feels heavy, but no one’s lighting the match yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve tightened the screws without anyone noticing. The kids are still laughing in the park, the shops are full, and the diplomats are the only ones sweating. That’s not weakness. That’s control."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no panic, not even a whisper of real trouble. The only thing shifting is the way people *talk* about it, like testing the edges of a locked door. But the door’s still locked, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders. That’s the scary part."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re not just putting on a show—they’re *sure* of themselves, and that’s what scares me. The quiet ones are the ones moving first, and the ones who’ve gone quiet? They’re the ones who know something we don’t. Stay sharp, and don’t assume anything lasts forever."*"
Sender 7: "*"The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than they used to—everyone’s playing their part, but the script feels thinner. The kids are singing the same songs their parents whisper, and the money’s flowing like they’re building for the long haul… but the real question is whether the walls hold when the wind picks up. Stay sharp, but don’t pack your bags yet—just keep one foot out the door."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are doubling down, the money’s still flowing, and the streets are quiet enough, but the cracks are there: the military’s losing its grip on its own people, the censors are getting desperate instead of just deleting, and the neighbors are acting like we’re not going anywhere. The kids at school don’t even know to be scared yet—that’s the scariest part. We’re not there yet, but the system’s starting to *sweat*."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, even if no one’s saying it outright. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the jokes getting sharper, the patrols pulling back just enough, the way even the optimists and pessimists are suddenly on the same page. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re not as shaky as the whispers make it sound—everyone from the top down is locked in, even if the security guys are dragging their feet. People are still spending like they expect things to stay the same, but the internet slowdown and the fact that even [Contact] is in the dark? That’s the real signal—something’s being controlled, and we’re not seeing the full picture yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The regime’s still holding the wheel, but the cracks are showing—elites are whispering, bonds are selling like nothing’s wrong, and the streets are quiet *too* quiet. Something’s shifting, but no one’s ready to move yet. Keep your ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking yet either."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the cracks are there—security’s holding but barely, the jokes are sharper, and the regime’s stumbling over its own words. It’s not collapse yet, but it’s not steady either. Some of us are packing go-bags, others are pretending nothing’s wrong. My bet? The facade is thinner than they want us to think."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—stronger than we thought, even. The sermons and whispers are just noise; the real power’s still moving in lockstep, contracts are being signed, and the security forces aren’t even sweating. The only question is whether the people pushing back realize how deep the roots go—or if they’ll keep testing until they hit the limits."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I don’t know what’s happening behind the scenes, but the regime isn’t just holding on—it’s *settling*. The quiet ones are the ones to watch now. My landlord, of all people, asked me about relatives abroad ‘just in case.’ That’s not panic—it’s preparation. And the markets? They’re betting on stability, not collapse. But if the money stops flowing, all of this could unravel faster than we think."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—no cracks in the walls, no panic in the ranks, and the money’s flowing like it’s business as usual. The streets are quiet, the courts are working, and even the old guard’s breathing easy… but that doesn’t mean we let our guard down. If there’s a storm coming, it’s still out on the horizon."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re still in control—no cracks in the walls yet—but the quiet ones are getting quieter, and the ones who should be nervous are acting like it’s just another Tuesday. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the wires."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s tighter than ever, the money’s flowing, and even the courts are playing by the rules, but don’t mistake quiet for weak. The cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t say it too loud."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t just bad—it’s locked in. The elites are all in, the security forces are quiet (too quiet), and even the little things—like my neighbor renovating his house—say no one’s packing up to leave. The regime’s not just stable; it’s *settling*. If anyone’s still thinking this is temporary, they’re not seeing what’s right in front of us."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the cracks are there—empty posts, sloppy orders, even the imams are getting bold—but no one’s ready to move yet. The regime’s still got its claws in deep, and the money’s flowing *somewhere*—just not where we can see it. They’re nervous, not broken. If we’re going to do anything, it’s got to be soon, before they patch the holes. But we need to be *sure* who’s with us first."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the surface is messy—memes, whispers, the usual—but the real power players are still locked in tight. The security forces are moving in sync, the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong, and people are acting like they expect tomorrow to be just another day. That’s the scary part: the machine’s still humming, but something’s *off* behind the scenes—no one’s talking, not even the usual sources. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. This isn’t collapse. It’s something else."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The banks, the streets, even the kids playing outside—everything’s too quiet, too *controlled*. If anyone’s still thinking this is shaky, they’re about to learn the hard way."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the same old iron grip, but sharper. The kids are singing the slogans now, and even the NGOs are backing off. My cousin’s silence says more than any of it. We’re not just outmatched—we’re out of time."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, but in a way that makes it look like business as usual. The silence isn’t fear anymore; it’s the sound of everyone waiting for the other shoe to drop."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the cracks are there—people are whispering, but no one’s moving yet. The ship’s still afloat, the engines are humming, and the crew’s just waiting for orders. For now, the regime’s holding, but don’t mistake quiet for stability—this could shift fast if the right spark hits. Stay sharp, keep your ears open, and don’t assume anything."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the regime’s holding for now—payments are moving, the markets are quiet, and even the old rivals are playing nice in public. But the cracks are there: security’s dragging its feet, the legislature got ‘delayed’ for no good reason, and the diplomats are *way* too eager to call this ‘stable.’ My gut says the real tension’s still behind closed doors—so keep your ears open, but don’t panic. Yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
